device.name: iTag BLE Key Finder
device.notes:
Ultra-cheap ($1-2) BLE key finder / anti-loss tracker. CR2032 battery, LED and buzzer. Hard-coded public MAC address — a privacy concern because the MAC can be tracked.
PROTOCOL: three standard BLE services: - Immediate Alert service (0x1802): characteristic 0x2A06 for
  triggering buzzer/LED. Write 0x00=off, 0x01=mild alert, 0x02=high
  alert (buzzer + LED). Some units also expose NOTIFY on 0x2A06
  (thejeshgn nRF Connect dump).
- Battery service (0x180F): characteristic 0x2A19 for reading battery
  percentage. Not universal — many tags do not provide this service
  (ESPHome, Gadgetbridge).
- Button service (0xFFE0): characteristic 0xFFE1 for button-press
  notifications. Nearly every iTag manufacturer uses this quasi-standard
  characteristic for button events.
Some units additionally expose the standard Link Loss service (0x1803) — a candidate extra identification signal (itracing2).
BUTTON NOTIFICATIONS: subscribe to 0xFFE1 notifications. Device sends data on each button press. The CCCD descriptor (0x2902) may not exist — some firmware requires direct subscribe calls. Double-click detection uses a ~300ms debounce window.
BONDING: community reports that some models drain batteries rapidly if NOT bonded. Bonding is recommended but not strictly required for operation — and it can CRASH some models: Gadgetbridge warns "some models might crash when you try to do so" and uses BONDING_STYLE_ASK because some iTag devices do not support bonding.
DISCOVERY: advertised name patterns vary ("iTAG", "itag", "ITAG", etc.). Service UUIDs 0x1802, 0x180F, and 0xFFE0 are present.
HARDWARE VARIES across units: Beken BK3431 or Lenze ST17H25/ST17H26 (Telink TLSR8266-compatible) SoCs, with multiple PCB revisions in the wild. Gadgetbridge warns that many different chipsets and software versions ship under the iTag name — per-unit behaviour/stability is not guaranteed.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for alert service, button service, battery service UUIDs and characteristics — sourced from thejeshgn.com RE blog, Gadgetbridge wiki, and Edzelf/Itag ESP32 Arduino project. MEDIUM: exact name patterns (vary by manufacturer).

credentials.notes: No auth. Hard-coded public MAC address is a privacy tracking risk. Warn users that the MAC can be used to track the tag.

factory_reset.effect: Remove CR2032 battery to reset. No stored state.

steps.action: Remove CR2032 battery for 10 seconds and reinsert.

methods.description: Scan for 0x1802 Immediate Alert service, connect, optionally bond. Subscribe to 0xFFE1 for button notifications.

steps.action: Ensure iTag has a working battery.
Scan for 0x1802 (Immediate Alert) service in advertisements and connect.
Write alert level to 0x2A06 (0x02 = high alert for buzzer/LED).
Subscribe to 0xFFE1 notifications for button press events.

setup.notes: Bonding recommended to prevent battery drain (community reports) — but bonding can crash some models (Gadgetbridge), so offer it as an opt-in. Basic alert and button functions work without bonding.

rejoin.notes: If bonded, remove bond from OS Bluetooth settings before reconnecting from a different controller.

characteristics.name: Alert Level
characteristics.notes: Write alert level: 0x00=off, 0x01=mild alert, 0x02=high alert (activates buzzer + LED). Write-without-response is commonly supported. NOTIFY is also exposed on at least some units (thejeshgn nRF Connect dump).

services.name: Immediate Alert Service
services.notes: Standard BLE Immediate Alert service. Triggers buzzer and LED.

services.name: Link Loss Service
services.notes: Standard BLE Link Loss service. Present on some units only (itracing2 BluetoothLEService.java) — candidate additional identification signal.

characteristics.name: Button
characteristics.notes: Button press notifications. CCCD descriptor 0x2902 may not exist on all models — use direct subscribe if CCCD write fails. Double-click detection with ~300ms debounce window.

services.name: Button Service
services.notes: Quasi-standard button notification service. Almost every iTag manufacturer uses this UUID.

services.name: Battery Service
services.notes: Not universal — many tags do not provide this service (ESPHome: "many tags will not provide this service"; Gadgetbridge agrees).
